content.text: The seat POST errors (108) have no matching server span, so the refused connection never reached a callee. I'll check which client spans lack a child server span, across services.

content.text: The drops are spread across many pods, so they don't isolate one pair. Connection-refused errors could also mean a callee pod restarted or disappeared, so I'll check restarts and pod uptime.

input.query: SELECT metric, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, COUNT(*) n, ROUND(MIN(value),1) mn, ROUND(MAX(value),1) mx FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE metric IN ('k8s.container.restarts','k8s.pod.uptime') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 80

content.text: ts-order-service's restart counter is at 1 throughout the abnormal window, and ts-ticket-office-service is at 2. I'll compare those counters with normal, and check order-service's uptime and class-loaded trend over time.

input.query: SELECT 'ab' per, time, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name pod, value FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name IN ('ts-order-service-668587b48c-z7r6g') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts') UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', time, metric, attr_k8s_pod_name, value FROM normal_metrics WHERE attr_k8s_pod_name IN ('ts-order-service-668587b48c-z7r6g') AND metric IN ('k8s.pod.uptime','k8s.container.restarts') ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 80

content.text: Order-service's restart counter went from 0 to 1 right at the start of the abnormal window, so the restart is real. Next I'll check whether the refused calls from seat and security cluster around that restart, using a per-minute timeline.

input.query: SELECT date_trunc('minute', c.time) m, c.service_name caller, c.span_name, COUNT(*) n, SUM(CASE WHEN c.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, ROUND(quantile_cont(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50 FROM abnormal_traces c LEFT JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' AND s.span_id IS NULL AND c.service_name IN ('ts-seat-service','ts-security-service') AND c.span_name IN ('POST','GET') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 40

content.text: The refused calls cluster in 08:43–08:45, right after order-service's restart at window start. That fits a short pod outage. Next I'll compare each service's own time (span duration minus child spans) between normal and abnormal, to check for other faults.

input.query: WITH base AS (SELECT 'ab' per, trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind kind, duration FROM abnormal_traces UNION ALL SELECT 'nm', trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, service_name, span_name, attr_span_kind, duration FROM normal_traces), ch AS (SELECT per, trace_id, parent_span_id pid, SUM(duration) cd FROM base GROUP BY 1,2,3), own AS (SELECT b.per, b.service_name, b.kind, b.duration - COALESCE(ch.cd,0) own FROM base b LEFT JOIN ch ON ch.trace_id=b.trace_id AND ch.pid=b.span_id AND ch.per=b.per WHERE b.kind='Server') SELECT service_name, SUM(CASE WHEN per='nm' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_nm, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='nm' THEN own END,0.95)/1e6,1) own_nm, SUM(CASE WHEN per='ab' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_ab, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='ab' THEN own END,0.95)/1e6,1) own_ab FROM own GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 LIMIT 60

content.text: The own-time figures are noisy because of parallel child calls, but ts-ui-dashboard stands out. I'll break down ui-dashboard's server spans by endpoint, normal versus abnormal.

input.query: SELECT span_name, SUM(CASE WHEN trace_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_ab, ROUND(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95_ab FROM abnormal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 25

SELECT span_name, COUNT(*) n_nm, ROUND(quantile_cont(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95_nm FROM normal_traces WHERE service_name='ts-ui-dashboard' AND attr_span_kind='Server' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 3 DESC LIMIT 25

content.text: Normal already has slow travel-plan and preserve endpoints, so I need to compare each key call edge between normal and abnormal. I'll compare caller-to-callee latency and errors on the edges that matter.

input.query: WITH j AS (SELECT 'nm' per, c.service_name caller, s.service_name callee, s.span_name, c.duration cd, s.duration sd, c.attr_status_code cs, s.attr_status_code ss FROM normal_traces c JOIN normal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client' UNION ALL SELECT 'ab', c.service_name, s.service_name, s.span_name, c.duration, s.duration, c.attr_status_code, s.attr_status_code FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces s ON s.parent_span_id=c.span_id AND s.trace_id=c.trace_id AND s.attr_span_kind='Server' WHERE c.attr_span_kind='Client') SELECT caller, callee, span_name, SUM(CASE WHEN per='nm' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_nm, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='nm' THEN cd END,0.95)/1e6,1) call_nm, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='nm' THEN sd END,0.95)/1e6,1) srv_nm, SUM(CASE WHEN per='ab' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) n_ab, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='ab' THEN cd END,0.95)/1e6,1) call_ab, ROUND(quantile_cont(CASE WHEN per='ab' THEN sd END,0.95)/1e6,1) srv_ab FROM j WHERE caller IN ('ts-travel-service','ts-travel-plan-service','ts-route-plan-service','ts-preserve-service','ts-security-service','ts-seat-service','ts-travel2-service','ts-ui-dashboard') GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 1,2 LIMIT 60

content.text: The main chain is now clear: travel-service's calls to seat fail or stall (p95 ~12 s), which slows travel-service's /trips/left, route-plan and travel-plan, and then ui-dashboard. kind_checks.scope: Affected: ts-order-service pod ts-order-service-668587b48c-z7r6g. Its restart counter moved 0 to 1 at the start of the incident, and its own Server spans and logs go silent from about 08:43:20 to 08:44:46 before recovering. Its callers that send to it (ts-seat-service POST, ts-security-service GET, and others) see failed client calls during that gap. Not affected: the order pod's metric rows keep arriving at normal volume through the gap, and normal memory is restored after the restart.

ruled_out.why: Normal container memory is steady at about 809 MB. In the abnormal window it reads about 261 MB in the 08:43 minute and climbs back to about 850 MB by 08:47. That is a reset followed by re-warming, not pressure building before the restart.

No heap or JVM memory metric was queried for the order pod. Its container and pod memory show a reset at the restart and a return to the normal level, with no climb toward a limit beforehand, so heap exhaustion is not supported by the data I did check.

A partition on the seat-to-order link would not silence the order service's own spans and logs for all callers. The order pod's Server spans and logs both stop entirely from about 08:43:20 to 08:44:46, which points to the process being down rather than one link being cut.

The order service recovers within the window: its Server spans return at 08:44:47 and its logs at 08:44:17, and the restart counter shows a restart with the same pod name. This is the pod_failure pattern. pod_unavailable is in the same equivalence class, so it would score the same, but the recovery argues against a permanent stop.

**Verdict: the evidence supports `pod_failure` for `ts-order-service`. Confidence is fairly high.** The equivalence class also accepts `pod_unavailable`, but the instance recovered within the window, so `pod_failure` fits.

**What supports it**

- **Restart with recovery.** The pod name stays `ts-order-service-668587b48c-z7r6g`. `k8s.container.restarts` is 0 in all 24 normal samples and 1 in all 24 abnormal samples, so the restart happened at the start of the incident window. The pod was not replaced: the name is the same and the counter moved.
- **A stop and a recovery.** The order service's own Server spans are absent from about 08:43:20 to 08:44:46, then return (first span at 08:44:47 and about 5 to 20 per second after). Its logs are absent from 08:43:20 to 08:44:17, then return at normal-ish volume. Its metrics keep arriving throughout (about 321 rows a minute before, 316 during).
- **Callers refused during the stop.** ts-seat-service POST client spans with Error status start at 08:43:20 and continue through the outage, at a few per second, with p50 about 480 ms. The seat log's 503 "Connection refused" errors fit this.
- **Memory reset, not memory exhaustion.** Normal memory is steady at about 809 MB. In the abnormal window it reads about 261 MB in the 08:43 minute and climbs back toward about 850 MB by 08:47. That is a reset followed by re-warming, not pressure building before the restart. CPU reads 3.6 cores at 08:44, against a normal 0.19, which is the start-up burst the guidance describes.

**What weighs against or limits it**

- The order service's spans and logs both go silent, and its own metrics continue. A partition of only the seat connection would not silence its traffic from other callers, so the whole-service silence points to the process, not the link.
- `k8s.pod.uptime` does not exist in either period for any pod, so I could not check the uptime reset. The restart counter is the only lifecycle signal.
- The metric rows show no gap during the outage. A container restart inside the same pod would explain that, but it is an inference, not something the telemetry states directly.
- The lead's "49 server spans in the 08:44 minute" is the same silence seen through the minute bucket: it reflects the roughly 85-second gap and the recovery at about 08:44:47.

**Other kinds I checked against**

- `container_memory_saturated` and `jvm_heap_exhausted`: ruled out. Memory was at its normal level before the restart, and it fell at the restart rather than climbing toward a limit beforehand.
- `network_partition`: unlikely. Order's own spans and logs stop entirely, not only for the seat link.
- `pod_unavailable`: ruled out by the recovery, though it is in the same equivalence class.
